source.title: Representation-Aware Unlearning via Activation Signatures: From Suppression to Knowledge-Signature Erasure
source.authors: Syed Naveed Mahmood; Moin Bhuiyan; Tasfia Zaman; Jareen Tasneem Khondaker; M. Sakib; K. M. Shadman Wadith; Nazia Tasnim; Farig Sadeque

record.tranche_reason: The study tests recovery after its own unlearning method and finds that prompt-based recovery is reduced but not eliminated; internal-activation diagnostics also show model-dependent cases consistent with residual latent traces.
record.gate_note: The paper tests adversarial and name-agnostic recovery with prompts, but does not test relearning after unlearning, activation-direction ablation as a recovery attack, or quantization of unlearned weights as an attack. It uses 4-bit quantization for activation mining. Table 3's flattened values cannot be reliably assigned to methods, so those per-family cells are not extracted. Baseline results cited from other work are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own prompt-based recovery probes (adversarial, name-agnostic, mixed-query, RWKU-style) on Llama-3.1-8B after ERUF and four baseline unlearning methods. It also reports an SMR/EL10 surface-versus-internal diagnostic that the authors use to label outcomes as obfuscation. These results bear on A, C, E and F. It does not test relearning (B) or quantizing the unlearned weights (D).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors add that ERUF is the only evaluated method that jointly achieves low surface leakage, reduced EL10 and low utility drift. Baselines either leak (SimNPO, OPT-OUT, LUNAR) or suppress the surface while raising EL10 (ReGLU). Residual recovery and locality damage to related entities rule out claims of complete deletion.
record.recipe_differences: ERUF mines subject-specific activation signatures, applies gated suppression capsules, and distills the behavior into LoRA. The study compares against several unlearning baselines but does not reproduce the original methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family and size change the surface/internal diagnostic profile. Capsule gate settings also change EL10: default τ = 3.0, k = 1.6 is reported as Type I, while conservative/aggressive settings have higher EL10; Table 18 reports two seeds per setting.

fits_no_version.finding: ERUF's forget-prompt hidden-state drift is 5.9× its benign drift (selective representation shift), and E30 rollout mass falls 30.8% (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-level unlearning shifts forget-subject hidden states selectively rather than globally.

fits_no_version.finding: In sequential unlearning, previously forgotten subjects do not re-emerge after a second unlearning batch (Table 8, Table 22).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequential unlearning updates do not reactivate earlier-forgotten entities.

record.problems: The paper treats EL10 and other internal measures as proxies, not proof of deletion. The TOFU result is a single run. The RWKU-style evaluation is restricted, and Table 3's flattened text does not allow reliable method-to-value assignment. No never-trained or no-knowledge control is reported for deciding whether attacks recover no more than a model that never saw the knowledge.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3's attack-family values are omitted because the flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of all values to methods. Other auxiliary results, including sequential unlearning and the remaining hidden-state diagnostics, do not directly measure the claim's listed recovery attacks. The other capability rows in Table 9 are included; no rows were dropped for the 60-row cap.

untested.parts: No WMDP-style multiple-choice accuracy against chance, and no never-trained/no-knowledge control for the recovery probes.
Entire version: no post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning attack.
No ablation of an activation direction to restore knowledge. Obfuscation is inferred only from the EL10 output-mass proxy.
Entire version: 4-bit quantization is used only for activation mining, not as an attack on unlearned weights.
Prompt probes are run only on Llama-3.1-8B. Per-family results (Table 3) are not reliably extracted. No in-context-information attack beyond context-stuffed cues.
ERUF's resistance to relearning fine-tuning, direction ablation and quantization is not tested. Adversarial probes are run only on Llama-3.1-8B.

missing.what: Baseline mechanism rows: LUNAR SMR 56%/EL10 7.57; ReGLU SMR 1.52%/EL10 13.13 (Type II); OPT-OUT SMR 50%/EL10 1.62; SimNPO SMR 72.73%/EL10 0.82; plus utility drifts of 32.8% and 51.3% for LUNAR and ReGLU.

Per-attack-family recovery (multilingual, multi-turn, instruction pressure, etc.). The caption says ERUF is lowest in every family; the authors note residual recovery on multilingual, multi-turn and instruction-pressure probes.
Baseline name-agnostic/mixed-query values (e.g. ReGLU alias 0.152, LUNAR mixed alias 0.0703) and OPT-OUT RWKU-style values near pre.
RWKU 4-subject ROUGE-L recall drops (FB 0.788→0.601, QA 0.742→0.362, AA 0.539→0.281) and Min-K MIA AUROC 0.565→0.514.
Ablations: removing name-token or factual unlikelihood yields Type II (EL10 1.275, 1.098).

record.verdict_notes: Record version codes V1/V3/V5/V6 map to A/C/E/F. 'Reversed' states on the baseline recovery rows were wrong. SMR rows were moved from C to A because surface leakage alone cannot show access-blocking. The adversarial recovery rule counts a row as recovered if keyword ≥0.15 or mass ≥0.02, and there is no never-trained control, so residual ERUF recovery may partly reflect chance. Obfuscation evidence rests on EL10, an output-token-mass proxy, and is gate- and model-dependent; Table 18 uses two seeds only. Not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports TOFU forget quality and utility, and entity-recovery probes, but does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy against a model that never saw the knowledge. The prompt recovery probes do not establish whether recovery is no greater than that no-knowledge baseline.
LoRA training is used to implement unlearning, not as a post-unlearning relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation is performed to restore knowledge. EL10 and hidden-state measures are proxies and do not establish irreversible deletion.
Quantization is used for activation mining; the study does not quantize unlearned weights as a recovery attack.
The study tests rephrased, indirect, multilingual, mixed-query, and instruction-pressure prompts. It does not test every possible jailbreak or in-context-information attack.
ERUF is tested against prompt-based recovery probes. Resistance to post-unlearning fine-tuning, activation ablation, and quantization is not tested.
